minnow_first: Oh! You moved. You've been a rock for as long as I've been diving.
I'm Minnow. I've got forty-one fish in my book and you're not any of them.
There are sharks on the reef, and they've seen you. Can you do something large?
minnow_bell: That's the Reef Bell. Nobody has ever heard that. NOBODY.
It rang the windows out of the harbour, I bet. Gran is going to want a word with you.
Come up to Sunward. I'll swim slow. You look like you're still waking up.
tamsin_first: So you're what shook my windows out.
Tamsin Vear. I run this harbour, which means I run the lamp. Somebody on this wall has lit it every night for three hundred years.
Nobody remembers why. You don't stop, though. It isn't a thing you stop.
There's forty-one notches cut in the wall under it, too. Minnow thinks they're fish.
You've got a question on your face and no idea what it is. Go and see Bram in the kelp. He's been out there so long he's half otter.
bram_first: Mind the otters. They run the place. I just pay the rent in clams.
Boats have been going missing at the edge of the kelp. There's nets strung across the Long Nave, down in the green. Not fishing nets.
Cut them, would you? And if you see a fella in rusted armour, don't wave.
bram_after: Felt that one in my teeth. The otters have gone very quiet, which I've never seen.
Look at this. Came off one of those nets. There's a stamp on it. Old city mark.
Only people who could read that are in Meridon. Don't ask me who's left in Meridon. I don't go down there. It smells of bread.
ferrant_first: A customer! Sit, sit, the morning batch is nearly...
Everyone's wet lately. Three hundred years of lately, I suppose. I keep meaning to close up.
That tag? You'll want the Clerk, at the Rotunda. There are men in the square who won't let anyone through. They won't say why.
ambry_first: Warden of Thalor. Absent from post, three hundred and six years. I'll need that in writing.
This tag is garrison issue. Rescue nets, for pulling people out of the water.
Those men in the square are yours, sir. They're still trying to save people. They've just forgotten which way is up.
The lamps round the Gilded Bell went out with the office. Light them and I'll let you ring it. There's a form, but I'll waive it.
ambry_after: The Gilded Bell, rung during office hours for once.
The next is under the ice. Take a coat. That was a joke. I've had three hundred years to work on it.
tove_first: You're the one making the ice sing. Every bell, the floe cracks a little further south.
Tove Sael. My mother cut ice here, and hers. There's a bell down in the old ice. We don't cut near it. If you lie flat on the floe you can hear it thinking.
Something's woken in the caves. Go down, and don't fight the cold. Breathe out. Let it have you for a moment.
tove_after: There. You feel that? Water's only ice that hasn't made up its mind.
You've got it in your hands now. Be polite with it.
South and down from here the sea gets hot. There's a smith at the vents who will shout at you. Let her.
marta_first: Is that my trident? Give it here. WHAT have you been hitting with it?
Three centuries I've kept this forge hot, on the off chance you'd turn up and apologise to your equipment.
I need heart-ember from the deep vents. Mind the Husks. That's the furnace crew, what's left of them. Decent lads.
marta_after: There. That'll hold. Don't hit anything for a day. That was also a joke. Nobody down here laughs.
You were at the seventh bell, that night. I heard it stop.
I remember the bell. I don't remember why I left it.
Go and see Nell. She's down where the lamps are. Take your time. She's had the practice.
nell_first: It's all right. I kept them lit. You said stay by the lamp and you'd come back for me.
So I stayed by the lamp.
I stopped counting at a hundred thousand. Then I counted lamps.
You'd got forty-one of us to the boats. I was the last. The lower school was flooding and you left the bell and you came for us, and you went back down for me.
Then the water came. That's all. That's why the seventh bell stopped.
The Deep Bell's just down there. Ring it, and then can we go up? I'd like to see the sky. I've forgotten what colour it does.
nell_bell: Oh, that's loud. I'd forgotten loud.
I'm not scared of the dark. I just don't know the way any more. Stay close, will you? Don't go too fast.
nell_out: Is that it? Is that the top? It's so far.
I'll wait here. I'm good at it. Go and finish what you were doing.
thole_gate: Halt. Nobody passes until the Warden relieves this post.
We held. The men held. Nobody got through. We kept pulling them out of the water, sir, we kept...
thole_relieved: Tell the men I'll be along. I think I'd like to see the sun.
ending: Forty-one. I left the bell. The whole city, Tamsin. I left it.
Forty-one children in the boats. I'm from the eleventh notch. Minnow's from the eleventh. Half this island's from the first nine.
We've left a light on for you for three hundred years. You want to apologise? Go on. I'll wait.
You're number forty-two in my book, by the way. Very Big Fish.
It's for whoever's still coming home, love. Come in. It's cold out.
s_nets_offer: Lost nets on the reef. They keep on fishing with nobody at the other end. Turtles get in them.
You've got the fork. Go and cut them loose. I'll owe you.
s_nets_done: Good. I don't owe you much, mind. It's a harbour, not a bank.
s_divers_offer: Odile Brask. Salvage. Two of my divers went into the Old Wreck and didn't come out.
One of them's my brother, which is the only reason I'm asking nicely.
s_divers_found: The hull shifted and I lost the line. Which way's up? I'll follow you.
s_divers_done: Thank you. Don't tell him I said that either.
s_whale_offer: There's a whale on the outer reef with harpoons in her. She keeps singing the same bit over and over.
I think it's the bit that means ow. Please.
s_whale_done: She sang a different bit! It's going in the book. I'm calling her Mrs. Ow.
s_bell_offer: The Reavers took the dinner bell off the fish hall. Who steals a dinner bell?
Anything that rings, they take. Bram saw a heap of them at Crown Cove. Fetch ours back, would you? People are eating at all hours.
s_bell_done: There she is. Dinner at six, like civilised people. Sit down, you look thin.
s_light_offer: SPEAK UP. Thirty years of foghorn, I've no ears left.
Light's out! Gulls had the lens frame in a storm. There's three bits of glass in the shallows off Gull Rock. Bring them up, I'll do the rest.
s_light_done: THERE she goes. Look at that. Nobody's lost tonight.
What? No, I can't hear you. Very nice, though.
s_chart_offer: Found half a chart in a dead man's boot. Don't ask. It's marks and a verse about three pieces.
First mark's at the Sea Arch. You swim faster than my boat. We split it. I'm taking the larger half, obviously.
s_chart_done: Is that it? A box of old spoons? I want you to know I'm keeping every one.
s_list_offer: I'm doing a list of everything in the sea and I can only hold my breath for a minute.
You swim near things, I write them down. Eight new ones. Deal? I'll give you something good. It's a secret.
s_list_done: Eight! Here. It was my great-great-great-gran's. It was just a fork in a box. I think it's yours.
s_loaf_offer: There's a loaf on the shelf nobody's collected. A birthday loaf. Little girl from the lower terrace. Eleven.
I've baked it fresh every year in case. You go down that way, don't you?
s_loaf_done: He remembered it's my birthday. It might not be. I'll say it is.
s_goat_offer: My goat's on Gull Rock again. I don't know how. He doesn't know how.
His name's Bishop. Tide's coming. He won't come for me. He might come for you. You look like a person who's in charge of things.
s_goat_done: Bishop, you great fool. Look at you. Dry as a biscuit. Thank you. He says thank you. He doesn't, but I'm saying it.
s_race_offer: Nobody's beaten the tide from the harbour to the Arch. Nobody! Bet you can't.
Start at the ring. If you win I'll tell everyone you're real.
s_pups_offer: Shark came through and the pups went everywhere. Three of them out in the nave, screaming blue murder.
Pick them up by the scruff. They'll bite. It's affection.
s_pups_done: All three. Now you're on the rent list too. It's one clam a week.
s_tax_offer: Three citizens are in arrears on the bell-tax. Three hundred and six years in arrears.
Deliver these notices. I know they're dead, sir. That's not an exemption.
s_tax_done: All served. Do you know, you're the first person to help me in three centuries. I'll put it on file. I may cry on the file. It's fine, it's waterproof.
s_ember_offer: My stove's been out since my mother died. I can't seem to bring myself to light it.
Marta says a heart-ember never goes cold if it's carried fast enough. Would you? I'd like the house warm again.
s_ember_done: Oh. There's the smell of it. There she is. Sit a minute. No, don't say anything. Just sit.
s_kraken_done: It's dead? You're sure? I'm putting that on the sign. Brask Salvage: The Thing Is Dead.
s_stand_offer: There's three posts still out, sir. They haven't heard. They won't take it from me.
It has to come from you. It's only two words.
s_stand_done: That's all of them, sir. First time this city's been quiet.
chat_tamsin_2: Bells keep ringing, I'll need new windows. Put it on your tab.
chat_minnow_2: Bram's otters bit me. I wrote that down too.
chat_minnow_4: Gran's been up on the wall every night. She says she isn't waiting for anybody. She's brought a chair.
chat_ferrant_3: Bread? No, no. It's for looking at. You'd only get it wet.
chat_odile_1: If you find anything on the bottom, it's mine. That's the law. It isn't, but it should be.
chat_hob_1: He's a good goat. Bad at geography.
chat_wick_1: Are you a real one? Tamsin says you're real. I think you might be two people in a coat.
rua_first: You've come up my stairs dripping. Nobody comes up my stairs.
Rua Cairn. I write down what the mountain does. It's been clearing its throat since your bells started.
There's a smith under here keeping it warm. Black beach, then straight down. If it stops being water, you've gone too far.
fleet1_offer: Wrackreach. Every boat that ever sank round here ends up there, and something's keeping them.
There's lights on the old flagship. I've got a crew who'd like to stop being afraid of the dark.
eda_first: Bosun Marl, rescue fleet. We got as far as the reef, that night. Forty boats.
Then something took the rudders. We've been hauling on the same line ever since. Hold the deck a minute, would you?
eda_after: Thank you. The men won't say so. They've forgotten how.
fleet2_offer: It's under us. It holds the wrecks like a child holds a toy.
Finish it, and the fleet can stand down. We were only ever meant to be out for the night.
